nodes.label: /news host-resolved public route family (ADR-0059)
nodes.rationale: Four routes, not seven: /news/feed.xml, /news/sitemap-news.xml and /news/search are deliberately absent because seo_distribution and site_search already serve those host-resolved at the root; a second copy would give one host two sitemaps and two places to enforce rssEnabled. /news rather than /blog/{slug} because Astro treats src/pages/blog/[slug].ts and blog/[tenantCode]/index.ts as the same pattern — the build only warns while one route silently shadows the other.

nodes.label: /blog/{tenantCode} legacy public route family (ADR-0009)
nodes.rationale: Kept fully supported for offline/LAN deployments with no domain/DNS/TLS; neither family redirects to the other. Known gap: it still has NO module-disabled check, so a tenant that disables blog_content can still be browsed through it.

nodes.label: withHostResolvedBlogTenant
nodes.rationale: Deliberately the same shape as site_search's withSiteSearchTenant and comments' withCommentsTenant (both modelled on seo_distribution's withSeoPublicTenant) — a fourth independently-written version of this rule would be a fourth place for it to drift. Every failure collapses to the same null and one generic 404.

nodes.label: padUnresolvedHostRouteLatency — timing parity as part of the gate
nodes.rationale: Without padding, an unresolved host costs zero round trips while a resolved one costs a transaction plus two queries, so latency alone answers 'does this hostname map to a live tenant?'. Padding runs against the all-zero fail-closed sentinel tenant, and the gate's two queries live in ONE function so a later edit cannot add a query to the serving path only.
nodes.norm_label: padunresolvedhostroutelatency — timing parity as part of the gate

nodes.label: Two public visibility predicates (listing vs detail)
nodes.rationale: Listing/search/feed/sitemap use visibility = 'public' strictly; detail uses visibility IN ('public','unlisted') — otherwise the 'unlisted' tier would be indistinguishable from 'private'. Both predicates live in public-blog-directory.ts, so a maintainer who disagrees changes one place, not seven route handlers.
nodes.norm_label: two public visibility predicates (listing vs detail)

nodes.label: renderContentJsonToHtml — whitelist block renderer
nodes.rationale: Every block type only ever emits text through escapeHtml; there is no 'raw html' block. Unknown types are skipped silently rather than throwing. Adding image/embed/table means a new switch case, never a raw-HTML escape hatch.

nodes.label: evaluateContentUpdateAccess — author-own-draft ABAC override
nodes.rationale: Expresses one permission as an OR: role permission, or (caller = authorTenantUserId AND status != 'published'). Deliberately NOT placed in identity-access's evaluateAccess — that evaluator is deny-biased and cross-module; an ownership-based ALLOW override is blog_content business logic layered on top of it, only reached when the sole deny reason is default_deny.

nodes.label: publicBasePath deliberately NOT adopted
nodes.rationale: An Astro file route cannot be repointed per tenant at runtime, so a configurable base path would change only the links a page emits while the serving route stays put — a per-tenant generator of URLs that 404. The physical root is the constant HOST_RESOLVED_PUBLIC_BASE_PATH; the only per-tenant choice is WHICH existing family is advertised.

nodes.label: rssEnabled/sitemapEnabled kept out of module-settings defaults
nodes.rationale: A second independently-writable copy in awcms_module_settings would let an admin flip RSS off in the generic module settings panel while the feed route keeps reading awcms_blog_settings and stays enabled — a correctness bug, not a style choice. An integration test PATCHes the key into the wrong store and asserts no effect.
nodes.norm_label: rssenabled/sitemapenabled kept out of module-settings defaults

nodes.label: Content quality checklist gate on publish/schedule
nodes.rationale: Server-side, not merely a client preview; no-op unless full-online R2-only mode is active for the calling tenant. Blocking failures answer 422 CONTENT_QUALITY_CHECKLIST_BLOCKED and are audited.
nodes.norm_label: content quality checklist gate on publish/schedule

nodes.label: publishDueScheduledPosts (bun run blog:publish:scheduled)
nodes.rationale: Restructured from one set-based UPDATE per tenant into SELECT ... FOR UPDATE plus a per-post loop so each due post passes the quality checklist; otherwise a tenant could bypass the checklist entirely by scheduling before enabling R2-only mode and waiting. FOR UPDATE also makes two concurrent workers safe. Blocked posts stay 'scheduled' and are audited, never silently published or unscheduled.

nodes.label: Append-only revisions and restore-as-new-revision
nodes.rationale: Restore writes the old content back through the ordinary update path and then records a NEW revision, so no row is ever UPDATEd or DELETEd and intermediate revisions stay readable. revisions.restore is explicitly required — no ownership override, unlike PATCH on the post itself.

nodes.label: parsePageParam/boundedPageNumber clamp on public ?page=
nodes.rationale: Unauthenticated route: ?page=1e8 became OFFSET 1e9 (Postgres scans and discards a billion rows while holding a pool connection — single-request DoS) and ?page=abc became OFFSET NaN → 500. Junk normalizes to page 1 rather than 400, because a broken ?page= on an HTML archive should render page one, not an error the crawler indexes.

nodes.label: resolvePublicContentBasePath — which family is advertised
nodes.rationale: Both families off means NO provider at all, so the sitemap/feed is empty rather than full of links certain to 404.

nodes.label: buildSocialShareLinks + expanded OG/Twitter metadata
nodes.rationale: Six-platform fixed allowlist, every URL encodeURIComponent-encoded; the canonical URL (never the request's raw querystring) is the only URL ever shared; the client script is a same-origin static file so it adds zero CSP surface.

nodes.label: /admin/blog lifecycle console (ADR-0051)
nodes.rationale: Three deliberate absences: no body editor (that is an editor, not a corner of a list), no posts.export button (the permission is seeded but NO endpoint enforces it, so the button would 404), and no search.read box (the admin list already searches by ILIKE, which tolerates the empty query websearch_to_tsquery rejects). Everything below the marker line in the README is awcms-mini SPECIFICATION, not this repo's code.

nodes.label: Two coexisting ad systems (awcms_blog_ads vs R2-only placements)
nodes.rationale: awcms_blog_ads.image_url accepts any http(s) URL — exactly the unmanaged-media hole media_library enforcement exists to close — while awcms_news_portal_ad_placements FKs a verified media object. ADR-0044 §4 decided to unify onto the FK'd table only after widening it with post/page targeting, so unification does not silently drop a capability. Until then, add no new users of awcms_blog_ads.
nodes.norm_label: two coexisting ad systems (awcms_blog_ads vs r2-only placements)

nodes.label: data_lifecycle module
nodes.rationale: Exists because every module was re-deriving retention semantics, batching, legal-hold interaction and safe deletion slightly differently; it adds a module-contributed registry plus a safe engine that operates on that contract and never on another module's schema.

nodes.label: HighVolumeTableDescriptor contract
nodes.rationale: Trusted code-only metadata — never tenant/request-controlled and never duplicated into a mutable settings table. Same 'module declares its own array, a central aggregator reads listModules()' shape as ModulePermissionDescriptor/ProjectionDescriptor.

nodes.label: executionMode: delegated vs generic
nodes.rationale: 'delegated' tables keep their own purge job as sole mutator and are only READ for dry-run backlog visibility; 'generic' tables opt into this module's own bounded engine. The one generic adopter is this module's own run-history table — dogfooding the engine on data it owns outright is the only way to prove non-delegated execution without reaching into another module's schema.

nodes.label: Legal holds override retention unconditionally
nodes.rationale: legalHold.applicable on a descriptor is documentation only and is deliberately NOT consulted by the enforcement path — an actual hold record targeting the descriptor key (or tenant-wide) always applies regardless of the descriptor's own claim, and no retentionDaysOverride can widen eligibility around it because the hold check runs first.

nodes.label: LegalHoldGuardPort — cross-module hold enforcement
nodes.rationale: A delegated adopter's OWN purge function is the real enforcement point because this engine never mutates a delegated table; the concrete adapter is wired at composition roots (audit-log-purge, visitor-analytics-purge, the retention purge route) and never imported inside logging/visitor_analytics' application/domain trees, which would close a forbidden import cycle (ADR-0011).

nodes.label: legal_hold.create and .release as separate permissions (SoD rule)
nodes.rationale: A role holding create does not implicitly hold release; the data_lifecycle.legal_hold_maker_checker SoD rule makes holding both a genuine critical conflict.
nodes.norm_label: legal_hold.create and .release as separate permissions (sod rule)

nodes.label: planLifecycleDryRun
nodes.rationale: Entirely SELECT count(*), zero mutation, so the on-demand endpoint needs no Idempotency-Key.

nodes.label: runDataLifecycleArchivePurge — bounded archive/purge engine
nodes.rationale: Archive writes happen OUTSIDE any DB transaction, then manifest + cursor advance in a new transaction; purge is a single-transaction bounded DELETE ... RETURNING covering only rows already archived. Legal holds are re-fetched per batch pass so a mid-backlog hold takes effect on the very next pass. Deliberately not exposed over HTTP — unattended maintenance, not a user action.

nodes.label: CURSOR_BOUNDARY_SAFETY_MARGIN_MS (timestamp precision)
nodes.rationale: timestamptz has microsecond resolution but a value read back through Bun.SQL as a JS Date has only milliseconds, truncating DOWN silently. Un-padded comparison permanently excluded the boundary row (one row short every cycle) and looped the archive resume on the same last row.

nodes.label: Provider-neutral ArchivePort + local adapter
nodes.rationale: read() never writes back into the source table; a real restore is a manual operator procedure that re-casts JSON/CSV-native types per column and INSERTs through the OWNING module's own code inside withTenant — the no-shared-table-write boundary applies during restore too. external_object_storage is valid typing with no adapter yet.

nodes.label: validateLifecycleRegistry (data-lifecycle:registry:check)
nodes.rationale: Pure, no I/O. legalHold.applicable:true MUST pair with precedence 'overrides_retention' — that cannot be declared away. Re-checked by security:readiness as defense in depth so it is visible from the go-live checklist, not only CI.

nodes.label: No shared-table write (ADR-0013 §6)
nodes.rationale: data_lifecycle owns exactly four tables and never writes another module's table directly, which is what forces the delegated/guard-port design instead of a central purge that reaches everywhere.

nodes.label: domain_event_runtime module
nodes.rationale: Transactional versioned outbox + dispatcher with per-order-key ordering (never a global total order), backoff, dead-letter and operator-safe replay.

nodes.label: appendDomainEvent — outbox producer
nodes.rationale: Called inside the producer's own business transaction (plain DB writes only, ADR-0006), so the event row and its per-consumer delivery rows commit atomically with the source state change — a rolled-back source transaction produces no dispatchable event by construction.

nodes.label: Versioned event-type registry
nodes.rationale: appendDomainEvent refuses to persist an event whose (eventType, eventVersion) is unlisted, stopping silent drift from the published AsyncAPI contract.

nodes.label: Static consumer registry (DOMAIN_EVENT_CONSUMERS)
nodes.rationale: A plain array so the full fan-out for any event type is knowable from source alone; fan-out is decided at PUBLISH time. Mini's later-wave consumers projecting into reporting/integration_hub were intentionally not ported because they would import absent modules.

nodes.label: Dispatcher (bun run domain-events:dispatch)
nodes.rationale: Claim/execute/finalize per consumer per tenant with head-of-line ordering per order_key; pure PostgreSQL/in-process with no external egress, so offline/LAN deployments are unaffected.

nodes.label: applyConsumerEffectOnce
nodes.rationale: Guarantees a consumer's side effect runs at most once per (consumer, event) under legitimate redelivery — the delivery guarantee stays at-least-once, never exactly-once.

nodes.label: Operator-safe delivery replay
nodes.rationale: Permission-gated, reason-required, Idempotency-Key-guarded, audited, and refuses replay against an incompatible consumer schema. The admin screen sends a key for replay but none for pause/resume, which are naturally idempotent — sending one would imply a replay contract the endpoint lacks.

nodes.label: Optional broker adapter port
nodes.rationale: A seam for future out-of-process delivery; no external broker is required or registered by default.

nodes.label: Global tables without tenant_id or RLS
nodes.rationale: Province 'Aceh' is the same row for every tenant; duplicating 91,599 rows per tenant would make storage grow with the customer list and make 'is every tenant on the same region version?' unanswerable. What replaces RLS is not trust: both tables are in GLOBAL_TABLE_FORBIDDEN_PRIVILEGES forcing explicit per-role privileges, neither app nor worker role holds DELETE, and every endpoint still runs session → tenant context → default-deny RBAC/ABAC. What is global is the ROW, not the authorization.
nodes.norm_label: global tables without tenant_id or rls

nodes.label: Dataset versioning: import → activate → rollback
nodes.rationale: Import writes a new dataset BESIDE the previous one, never over it, which is what makes rollback a status flip instead of a re-import. A new dataset always lands 'validated', never 'active' — importing is a deployment step, choosing what is SERVED is an audited operator decision. Only one active dataset, enforced by a partial unique index rather than an application check two concurrent requests could interleave through.

nodes.label: Import validation refuses partial hierarchies
nodes.rationale: Grammar mismatch, duplicate code, absent parent, an empty tier, or a checksum mismatch each fail the whole import rather than importing what it could — a hierarchy missing its middle breaks pickers invisibly, and recorded provenance that does not match the bytes is fiction.

nodes.label: source-provenance.ts — the not-official-Kemendagri caveat
nodes.rationale: Data is a community packaging (cahyadsn/wilayah, MIT) of the Kepmendagri decree, not an official API/export. The caveat lives in exactly one file and is re-read by the dataset API response and the admin screen, so the three can never drift.

nodes.label: Activation/rollback demoted to operator jobs (ADR-0052)
nodes.rationale: They changed the dataset served to EVERY tenant, but their permissions were seeded into the global catalog that setup/initialize grants wholesale to each tenant's owner — so an ordinary tenant owner held authority over data served to other tenants. With no tenant_id and no RLS there is no tenant the action belongs to, so no tenant permission can honestly express it. Also: no import permission (import is a job, and seeding one would advertise a surface that does not exist).

nodes.label: authorizeInTransaction — the single authorization chokepoint
nodes.rationale: Checks resolveModuleEnabled BEFORE permission lookup, so a module disabled for a tenant is denied 403 MODULE_DISABLED whatever permissions the actor holds, and the denial is still recorded in the decision log. Because every protected endpoint uses this guard, one check closes every endpoint of a disabled module without touching any route; module_management is isCore so a tenant can never lock itself out of re-enabling.

nodes.label: evaluateAccess — default deny, deny overrides allow
nodes.norm_label: evaluateaccess — default deny, deny overrides allow

nodes.label: Guards must use SEEDED catalog actions
nodes.rationale: The catalog seeds identity_access.access_control with only read/assign/configure. Owner is granted every catalog row at bootstrap, so a guard naming an unseeded action denies even the owner — which is why role/policy/user writes all gate on 'configure' rather than create/update/delete.
nodes.norm_label: guards must use seeded catalog actions

nodes.label: Dynamic ABAC policy evaluator (ADR-0033)
nodes.rationale: Conditions are a bounded jsonb AST interpreted purely — no eval/new Function/dynamic import/SQL. Attributes come from a server-side allow-list checked by own-property only, so prototype keys cannot slip through. Precedence is fail-closed: explicit DENY (or an invalid active policy, or ANY evaluation error) wins before RBAC is even checked; allow never creates permission; applicable allows act as a constraint that must be satisfied.

nodes.label: is_dsl_managed discriminator between the two authoring surfaces
nodes.rationale: The old flat surface carries only effect/description/is_active and cannot be scoped or conditioned, so evaluating a flat 'deny' would be wildcard + always-true = deny EVERY request = a bricked tenant with no in-band recovery. Only the DSL surface sets is_dsl_managed = true, and the evaluator filters is_active AND is_dsl_managed. The validator additionally rejects an unscoped + unconditional deny on both surfaces.
nodes.norm_label: is_dsl_managed discriminator between the two authoring surfaces

nodes.label: Tenant-keyed ABAC policy cache
nodes.rationale: Compiled once per tenant and invalidated deterministically AFTER commit by every create/update/enable/disable from both surfaces. Known limit: invalidation is per-process, so multi-instance needs LISTEN/NOTIFY or a TTL.

nodes.label: Business-scope hierarchy (ADR-0030 / ADR-0060)
nodes.rationale: scope_type/scope_id are generic references, not FKs to an organization table; validity and ancestry resolve through BusinessScopeHierarchyPort, now provided by tenant_admin against awcms_offices (live rows only, depth-bounded, cycle-safe). Fail-closed: unknown/unresolved/stale hierarchy denies high-risk actions, and resolved:false is NOT the same as 'resolved with no ancestors'. Every subject/role/actor FK is COMPOSITE (tenant_id, …) because PostgreSQL RI checks bypass RLS, so a single-column FK could point across tenants even under FORCE.

nodes.label: Segregation of duties layer (ADR-0031)
nodes.rationale: The base hard-codes NO domain rules — rules flow in from owning modules' descriptors via listModules(), and illustrative examples live in a test fixture. Enforced at two points: assignment-time rejection and fail-closed action-time checking, because a conflict must be caught at EXECUTION, not only at assignment. Facts merge business-scope and ordinary RBAC grants; without a requestedScope the result is INDETERMINATE, which defaults to deny. Exceptions are scope-bound, time-bound, revocable, critical-audited and can never be self-approved.

nodes.label: MFA TOTP, recovery codes and step-up (ADR-0027)
nodes.rationale: AUTH_MFA_ENABLED gates only ENROLLMENT; challenge/disable/step-up are driven by database state (an active factor row), so turning the flag off can never let an already-enrolled identity skip the second factor. Anti-replay is a compare-and-swap on last_used_step, so the loser of two same-timestep requests updates zero rows and is rejected; recovery codes use the same CAS on used_at. The MFA branch is only reached AFTER the password is valid, so it adds no enumeration oracle. Encryption key has no default — a missing key fails closed.
nodes.norm_label: mfa totp, recovery codes and step-up (adr-0027)

nodes.label: OIDC/SSO tenant-aware login and account linking (ADR-0028)
nodes.rationale: Provider config is per-tenant DATA, not env. A successful OIDC login mints an opaque AWCMS session — the ID token is never used as the session. No auto-linking merely because emails match; linking requires a valid session AND a fresh step-up. JIT provisioning creates identities at minimum privilege.
nodes.norm_label: oidc/sso tenant-aware login and account linking (adr-0028)

nodes.label: SSRF guard for discovery/JWKS/token fetches
nodes.rationale: HTTPS-only, blocks private/loopback/link-local/ULA/CGNAT/metadata ranges for IPv4 and IPv6 including IPv4-mapped and NAT64, validates every DNS result before connecting, follows redirects manually with re-validation per hop, and caps time and response size. This deliberately REVERSES awcms-mini's risk-acceptance decision.

nodes.label: Break-glass access and its drift-after-save gap
nodes.rationale: sso_required / password_login_disabled require at least one active break-glass owner at SAVE time — but eligibility is a property of identities/tenant_users, not of the policy, so deactivating that user through ordinary user administration silently invalidates a stored policy without the policy being touched. security-readiness re-derives eligibility per active tenant using the SAME functions (not a copy of the rule), one withTenant per tenant because the policy table is FORCE RLS.
nodes.norm_label: break-glass access and its drift-after-save gap

nodes.label: Password reset by email
nodes.rationale: Enumeration-safe by construction: unknown identifier, inactive identity/tenant-user/tenant, SSO-only identity and non-email identifiers all return the identical 'ineligible' body, and every failure mode on redemption collapses to one error code so the endpoint is not a token-status oracle. Single-use is enforced by FOR UPDATE in the DATABASE — without the row lock two redemptions of the same link both saw used_at IS NULL and both succeeded (proved red by mutation). The SSO-only policy is re-read at redemption so a live link does not survive a tenant disabling password login. Delivery goes through the auth_notification capability port because identity_access must not write the email module's table, and email already depends on identity_access so a dependency edge would close a cycle.

nodes.label: Self-registration with admin approval
nodes.rationale: OFF by default and answers 404 when off — the same answer as a route that does not exist, so the switch cannot be found by probing. It never creates an account and never accepts a password: approval creates an identity with a discarded random password and sends a reset link, so the applicant proves mailbox control, rejected requests leave no credentials, and a spam flood is not a flood of argon2id hashes (a deliberate divergence from awcms-micro, which stored an anonymous submitter's chosen hash). approve and reject are separate permissions; approval locks the row FOR UPDATE with a status='pending' predicate so a concurrent second reviewer gets a clean 404 instead of a 23505-induced 500.

nodes.label: Machine credentials (ADR-0049)
nodes.rationale: A build cannot hold a session token — sessions expire, are revoked wholesale on password reset, and rotate on step-up — so awcms-astro could not fetch its own content. The token carries its own tenant, and hashSessionToken DISPATCHES on the token prefix so 183 existing routes gain the behaviour with no signature change. It AUTHENTICATES only: the module-enabled → RBAC → ABAC → decision-log → SoD chain runs unchanged. Read-only is enforced before permissions are consulted, and allowed_permission_keys only NARROWS by intersection. Deactivating the service account kills the credential immediately — stricter than the session path deliberately, because otherwise 'deactivate this account' would leave a working key for months. Issuance is deliberately NOT idempotency-keyed, since replaying it would mean storing the plaintext token.

nodes.label: Session handoff for a cross-origin BFF (ADR-0050)
nodes.rationale: The awcms session cookie belongs to the awcms origin and must not cross it. Proxying the login form was rejected twice: the password would cross a repo that is not the identity store, and login is not one step (it can answer MFA_REQUIRED, redirect to a tenant's OIDC provider, or demand a Turnstile token) so proxying means a second copy of MFA, OIDC callback and Turnstile. Issue is self-service (identity and assurance come from the SESSION, never the body — inventing a permission here is the latent-authz trap this repo has already shipped twice); redeem is the only client-credential-authenticated endpoint, because it is the request that OBTAINS a session. redirect_uri is EXACT-match allow-listed, not prefix (app.example.com prefixes app.example.com.evil.test) and not origin-only; query and fragment are rejected rather than stripped. The code stores no live credential, assurance never rises, single use is a conditional UPDATE ... WHERE redeemed_at IS NULL, and used rows are KEPT so replay is answered from evidence rather than from absence of evidence.
nodes.norm_label: session handoff for a cross-origin bff (adr-0050)

nodes.label: /admin/security policy console
nodes.rationale: Adds no enforcement — every mutation posts to the original endpoint. Its gates use the endpoints' EXACT permission keys, including mfa_admin.reset as the MFA READ gate, which looks wrong but is what the endpoint demands; inventing an unseeded mfa_admin.read would be the latent-authz trap that has bitten this repo twice. Deployment posture is shown read-only so a contradiction like ssoRequired with AUTH_SSO_ENABLED=false surfaces as a warning instead of silence. The break-glass picker uses IDENTITY ids because both are uuids and the wrong one is accepted and then filtered to an empty list — a silent no-op exactly where the operator is trying to keep themselves able to log in.

nodes.label: Login audit and anti-enumeration hardening
nodes.rationale: login_failed is written in the same transaction as the failed-count UPDATE so it commits together, which is what stops the success-path reset of failed_login_count from erasing the preceding brute-force trail. Attributes never include the raw IP or the login identifier (storing an attacker's string on failure creates its own enumeration leak); ipHash is a keyed HMAC. Unknown identifiers still pay one argon2id verify against a constant dummy hash to remove a ~75 ms timing oracle, and 'locked' answers identically to 'invalid_credentials'. Env thresholds parse through parsePositiveIntEnv because a NaN threshold makes count >= NaN always false and silently disables lockout.

nodes.label: Bun.SQL does not bind JS arrays as Postgres arrays
nodes.rationale: ${["a","b"]} arrives as the text 'a,b' (22P02 malformed array literal), and the single-element form is the most dangerous because it arrives as 'a' and looks like an ordinary string. Use toPostgresTextArray(...)::text[].
nodes.norm_label: bun.sql does not bind js arrays as postgres arrays

nodes.label: now() DEFAULT is the transaction-start instant
nodes.rationale: created_at DEFAULT now() and an expires_at derived from the application clock are two different clocks, so a CHECK tying them together rejects perfectly normal rows once the transaction has been open a moment. The application writes both from one clock. Found by an integration test, not by reading.
nodes.norm_label: now() default is the transaction-start instant

nodes.label: Ownership inversion out of news_portal (ADR-0036)
nodes.rationale: news_portal owned the registry only because the epic that needed media happened to be the news portal, so a brochure-site tenant had no managed media at all. The coupling lived in the port contract itself (isFullOnlineR2ModeActiveForTenant is an editorial question), so the port was SPLIT rather than renamed. The table name awcms_news_media_objects was deliberately kept: a hard composite FK plus three migrations reference it.

nodes.label: Managed-media enforcement is one-way by construction
nodes.rationale: There is no disable action, no unmark function and no DELETE against the state table anywhere — a tenant able to switch its own media validation off is a confirmed-exploitable hole. The only rollback is a deployment-level R2 config change, fail-closed via readiness. Two halves must both hold: deployment readiness (pure function) and per-tenant opt-in written by a single sanctioned entry point.
nodes.norm_label: managed-media enforcement is one-way by construction

nodes.label: Object lifecycle: delete / restore / purge (ADR-0056 §B)
nodes.rationale: Three permissions sat in the catalog granted to every owner and enforced by NOTHING — the functions behind them had zero callers, so an orphaned or policy-violating object only vanished if the reconciliation job happened to categorise it. Soft delete deliberately breaks live references (a policy-violating image must stop being served) and restore is why that is recoverable; none of the endpoints scans for referencing rows first, because that would make the module know its own consumers. purge clears the REGISTRY only — the reconcile job owns R2 and a second writer would mean two processes with different ideas of what is safe to remove.

nodes.label: 409 MEDIA_OBJECT_REFERENCED via savepoint + errno SQLSTATE
nodes.rationale: In PostgreSQL a 23503 aborts the whole transaction, so catching it without a savepoint turns a caller-actionable 409 into a 500 at COMMIT. The SQLSTATE must be read from error.errno — Bun puts its own constant on error.code, so comparing code to "23503" can never be true.

nodes.label: GET /api/v1/media/objects/list — keyset browse
nodes.rationale: The application layer had only point lookups, so no browse screen could be built whatever the permissions said. Kept separate from GET /media/objects because that endpoint demands ?ids= as a batch RESOLVER — teaching it a no-ids mode would turn a request that 400s today into a dump of the whole registry, a contract change dressed as an addition. It deliberately outgrows the resolver's safety rule (any status, optionally soft-deleted) because an administrator opens the list precisely for the objects that are NOT healthy. The cursor carries full-precision created_at TEXT, never a JS Date: a batch upload writes many rows inside one millisecond, and reverting to a Date loses 57 of 107 test rows.

nodes.label: resolveMediaReferences / GET /api/v1/media/objects
nodes.rationale: The registry previously had no read surface at all, so an out-of-process consumer could see that a post HAS an image but had no way to learn its URL — awcms-astro returned src: undefined and every article published without its image while nothing failed. Unresolved ids are REPORTED rather than dropped, because returning only successes makes 'this resource has no image' and 'its image reference is broken' the same response — the ambiguity that let the gap persist. Non-uuid ids are 400, since 'you sent junk' and 'that object may not be referenced' are different facts. Read-only, so machine credentials may hold it.

nodes.label: /admin/media console and its three deliberate absences
nodes.rationale: No upload (a three-step browser flow whose half-finished sessions would leave a pending_upload row on every misclick — exactly the litter reconciliation cleans up), no enforcement toggle (a tenant-wide one-way policy switch belongs on /admin/security), and no preview (a row may be pending or failed, and rendering it shows a policy-violating image one more time to the person removing it). Pinned by a contract test so these stay decisions rather than becoming gaps.
nodes.norm_label: /admin/media console and its three deliberate absences

nodes.label: maskIdentifierValue — two masking shapes
nodes.rationale: Email-shaped values keep the domain and first local character so an admin can still tell outbox/suppression rows apart; everything else keeps only the last four characters, and nothing at all at four characters or fewer. The email branch is detected from the VALUE, not from a type argument, because the email module masks addresses that are never profile identifiers and has no IdentifierType to pass.

nodes.label: 23505 → DuplicateIdentifierError → 409 inside withTenant
nodes.rationale: The unique-violation must be translated to 409 INSIDE withTenant — if it escapes, the error is no longer a PostgresError and starts counting toward the database circuit breaker.

nodes.label: POST /api/v1/profiles/{id}/restore
nodes.rationale: delete_reason is deliberately preserved — the reason for deletion stays true after restoration, and restored_at is what says it no longer applies. The precondition lives in the WHERE clause rather than a read-then-write, since two concurrent restores that both read first would both proceed and write two audit rows for one recovery. A missing profile and a non-deleted profile answer the SAME 404, because a distinguishable answer makes the route a profile-id oracle.

nodes.label: createPersonProfileForIdentity — the single writer
nodes.rationale: awcms_identities.profile_id is NOT NULL, so creating a login structurally requires a profile. Each creating path used to write its own row and they had ALREADY diverged: SSO JIT set verification_status='verified' while self-registration approval left the default, so two accounts minutes apart got different verification postures with nobody deciding. Now emailVerified is explicit and false means no proof of mailbox control — a reviewer's say-so is not proof, the reset link the approval sends is. It deliberately writes no audit event, because the caller owns the audit for the real decision.

nodes.label: Five generic live-aggregation reporting views
nodes.rationale: No new tables — all five read tables other modules already own. One permission (reporting.dashboard.read) covers all five, deliberately not split per view. Unknown modules get 'No metric defined yet' instead of an error so module-usage stays generic against future modules. Deliberately no worker/materialized view/cache: latency follows query cost, and optimisation was left out of scope.

nodes.label: ProjectionDescriptor contract
nodes.rationale: Same module-declares-its-own-array shape as dataLifecycle and sodRules. The engine never writes another module's transactional table — it reads a source and writes only its own awcms_reporting_projection_* tables.

nodes.label: cursor_table vs domain_event projection strategies
nodes.rationale: cursor_table can only ADD, so it is correct only for a genuinely append-only source; that is why the ABAC decision log and identity/sync-node counts were wrapped and sync-health/email-health/office-and-profile counts (mutable state or soft-delete-with-restore) were NOT — those need row-level CDC. domain_event reuses domain_event_runtime's jobs/locks/batching/idempotency/retry/pause machinery instead of building a second one. Regardless of steady-state strategy, every projection REBUILDS through the same bounded cursor re-scan against the authoritative source.

nodes.label: Idempotent, resumable projection rebuild
nodes.rationale: Exactly one place resets cursors/metrics to zero, done in the caller's own transaction atomically with the run row, audit log and idempotency record; a partial unique index makes a concurrent double-reset impossible at the database level and INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING keeps a lost race from poisoning the transaction. Continuation NEVER resets — one bounded pass is one transaction, so a crash leaves everything consistent at the last completed pass. While a rebuild owns a projection the cursor_table worker skips it (the rebuild's own re-scan shares the cursor), whereas the domain_event consumer THROWS and defers, then on retry compares the event's occurredAt against the rebuild watermark — a plain skip-with-retry would either lose an event permanently (rebuild cancelled first) or double-count it (rebuild completed).

nodes.label: pg_advisory_xact_lock per (tenant, projection)
nodes.rationale: Taken as the FIRST statement of every transaction that writes a projection's cursor/metric rows — this is what makes rebuild and steady-state mutually exclusive.

nodes.label: computeProjectionFreshness — computed live, never cached
nodes.rationale: A PURE function of persisted facts versus now, never a stored status enum — so if the worker stops entirely and no write ever happens again, the READ path still ages the status current → delayed → stale from elapsed time alone. rebuilding always wins; failed is checked after it.

nodes.label: reconcileProjection — fresh control total
nodes.rationale: On-demand only and needs no Idempotency-Key (it mutates no business state, only appends history) — the same posture data_lifecycle's dry-run already set. A mismatch while merely 'delayed' is EXPECTED: read freshness alongside reconcile, never instead of it.

nodes.label: Scheduled projection exports
nodes.rationale: Deliberately minimal rather than built on data_exchange, whose staged-import machinery fits arbitrary business-record export, not a small metric snapshot. Artifacts are written OUTSIDE any DB transaction, SHA-256 checksummed, CSV formula-injection neutralised; download re-checks RBAC/ABAC and tenant scope at DOWNLOAD time and 410s an expired artifact. Two admitted gaps: the returned checksum header is the stored manifest value rather than recomputed from the bytes read, and `filter` is persisted but never applied — so a non-empty filter is REJECTED with 400 NOT_IMPLEMENTED rather than silently ignored, which would give a false sense of scoping.

nodes.label: Two enforcement layers for reading a projection
nodes.rationale: The route's coarse gate is necessary but not sufficient: each descriptor declares its OWN requiredPermission, additionally enforced by a filter — the same pattern navigation-registry uses for admin nav. All three current descriptors share a permission so the second layer is not yet distinguishable, but it is what stops a coarse-permission holder from seeing a future narrower-permissioned projection.
nodes.norm_label: two enforcement layers for reading a projection

nodes.label: /admin/reporting console
nodes.rationale: Every mutation goes through the real endpoints — no privileged shortcut, no SQL in the page. It also renders email-health, the one dashboard view /admin never picked up; duplicating it onto /admin was deliberately declined (one view, one place).

nodes.label: README previously described screens that never existed here
nodes.rationale: The /admin/reporting/projections tree and a submitJson helper came over with the port and were never true in this repo. Because the module declared no navigation entry, the registry gate that catches a dangling path had nothing to check — docs are not gated the way descriptors are.
nodes.norm_label: readme previously described screens that never existed here

nodes.label: seo_distribution module
nodes.rationale: A CONSUMER/aggregator of SEO facts, never a provider: content modules provide seo_facts and this module composes them. Nothing in the base registry depends on it and its lifecycle dependencies are only the two Core modules, so the module DAG is untouched.

nodes.label: Central <head> renderer (seo-document + seo-head-rendering)
nodes.rationale: One deterministic head from resource facts + tenant defaults + the server-derived primary host. Degrades to a relative canonical when there is no primary domain rather than inventing a host (offline-LAN safe). Resource facts win over tenant defaults; og:url is the canonical.

nodes.label: seo_facts capability contract
nodes.rationale: blog_content is the base's single declared provider; a future content type ships its own adapter and seo_distribution never learns that type exists. Only one module may declare provides: [seo_facts] at a time, enforced by capability_provider_conflict.

nodes.label: isPubliclyResolvable / isPubliclyIndexable
nodes.rationale: Draft/scheduled-future/archived/deleted/private resources are not renderable at all; a resolvable-but-noindex resource renders with robots: noindex and carries NO structured data. There is no code path that emits an unpublished resource to public output.

nodes.label: Public discovery surfaces (robots/sitemap/feeds)
nodes.rationale: Astro XML/text routes at the host root, not OpenAPI. Tenant-wide noindex suppresses ALL of them, not just robots.txt, so non-robots-respecting scrapers get no machine-readable URL enumeration. With no active primary domain the sitemaps and feeds 404 (their <loc>/<id>/<guid> must be absolute) while robots.txt still serves 200 minus its Sitemap: line. Everything is bounded — the index sizes from one aggregate, each child is one window, feeds are capped.

nodes.label: Host is server-derived, never taken from the request
nodes.rationale: Canonical/OG/hreflang hosts come from the tenant's verified primary domain; the renderer never reads Host or X-Forwarded-Host — the host-header-poisoning defence.
nodes.norm_label: host is server-derived, never taken from the request

nodes.label: renderControlledJsonLd — injection blocked by closed schema
nodes.rationale: A closed @type/key schema plus escaping of <>& and U+2028/U+2029, rather than ad-hoc sanitization; no hand-serialized JSON-LD exists anywhere, and structured data is emitted only for indexable resources.
nodes.norm_label: rendercontrolledjsonld — injection blocked by closed schema

nodes.label: buildDiscoverySignature — ETag/Last-Modified validators
nodes.rationale: Deterministic signature over kind + tenantId + host + locale + contract version + config fingerprint + content roll-up, NUL-joined so free-text parts cannot merge across their boundary, and tenant-first so tenants sharing the null-host sentinel stay isolated. Because validators derive from content/domain/config state, any publish/update/archive/delete/domain/locale/config change invalidates the affected output.

nodes.label: withSeoPublicTenant + padUnresolvedSeoTenantLatency
nodes.rationale: Server-controlled host resolution, host trusted only behind a trusted proxy, module-enabled gate, and every non-serving outcome collapsing to one generic latency-normalized 404.

nodes.label: Redirect governance (ADR-0039)
nodes.rationale: Exact-path rules resolved in middleware on the non-/admin branch before content routing, excluding admin/API/auth/static/system/discovery paths at BOTH resolve and write time; chains are bounded, non-recursive and fail CLOSED on loop or over-cap. The one invasive middleware edit is FAIL-OPEN — the resolver swallows faults to null and never 500s, and 404 capture never throws. 404 telemetry is privacy-minimized to a sanitized path plus bare referrer domain, with its own data_lifecycle descriptor.

nodes.label: redirect-target-classification — frozen open-redirect guard
nodes.rationale: Re-homed as a standalone domain helper rather than re-added to the seo_facts port, and applied on write AND on every resolve.

nodes.label: Permission backfill only reaches tenants created after the migration
nodes.rationale: Seeding into the global catalog means only tenants created AFTER that migration get the permissions — a functional (not security) release step.
nodes.norm_label: permission backfill only reaches tenants created after the migration

nodes.label: HMAC signature v2 binds tenant and node
nodes.rationale: v1 signed only timestamp.body, binding neither tenant nor node, so it is cross-tenant forgeable and is kept only for already-deployed nodes; the advisory closes only when SYNC_HMAC_ALLOW_LEGACY=false AND every node is on v2. v2 requires tenantId to be a UUID, because node_code may contain ':' and a non-UUID tenant would make the tenant/node boundary ambiguous in the signed material — a UUID is fixed-length with no colon, so compute throws and verify fails closed on anything else.
nodes.norm_label: hmac signature v2 binds tenant and node

nodes.label: First-contact nodes auto-register INACTIVE
nodes.rationale: An admin must approve a node before it can push/pull, which quarantines a forged first-contact node id for another tenant; deactivation takes effect immediately across push/pull/status/objects.

nodes.label: Generic optimistic-concurrency conflict tracking
nodes.rationale: Two domain-agnostic conflict types (missing_base_version, version_mismatch); conflicting events go to sync_conflicts rather than the inbox and do NOT advance the aggregate version. Conflict resolution endpoints are session-authenticated rather than HMAC, because resolving is a human decision, not a node action.

nodes.label: Object sync queue and retry policy
nodes.rationale: requires_upload is set from R2_ENABLED at enqueue time as a DATA flag, never a network trigger (ADR-0006). Re-enqueuing the same objectKey upserts and resets to pending rather than duplicating. Checksum comparison is plain string equality — a checksum is not a secret.
nodes.norm_label: object sync queue and retry policy

nodes.label: dispatchObjectSyncQueue — three-phase claim/upload/finalize
nodes.rationale: Required by ADR-0006: never call a provider inside a transaction. Claim flips rows to a transient status with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, reusing next_retry_at as a claim lease so no new column was needed; upload happens outside any transaction; finalize is a second short transaction. Naturally idempotent because sent/failed rows are never re-claimed and the destination objectKey is itself the dedup key. A per-provider circuit breaker skips only requires_upload=true rows.

nodes.label: /admin/sync operator console
nodes.rationale: None of the three mutations sends an Idempotency-Key because none of the endpoints requires one — all three are naturally idempotent state transitions — and a contract test pins that in BOTH directions so an endpoint that later starts requiring a key turns the screen red instead of failing at runtime. The HMAC node protocol gets no controls here and will not: those authenticate a node by signature, not an administrator by session.

nodes.label: theming module
nodes.rationale: The first website module implemented directly in the awcms base — the evidence for ADR-0034's 'template dipakai-langsung' decision that superseded the old no-content-website-modules restriction.

nodes.label: Trusted build-time theme vs tenant-authored ThemeConfig
nodes.rationale: A theme is reviewed in-repo code bundled at build time; tenant authorship is DATA only (token overrides, slot selections, media ids, section order). There is no database-stored executable template anywhere, and no uploaded code, arbitrary templates or raw CSS/HTML/JS.
nodes.norm_label: trusted build-time theme vs tenant-authored themeconfig

nodes.label: css-value-validation — reject, never sanitize
nodes.rationale: Charset-limited, length-bounded, control-char-free, rejecting url( / expression / @import / javascript: / comment openers / ;{}<> / backslash / unbalanced parens. Rejecting rather than stripping sidesteps the incomplete-multi-character-sanitization class entirely. Grammars are strict and linear (no ReDoS); font families come from a per-theme allow-list so no font value is ever tenant-authored.

nodes.label: Tokens served as an external same-origin stylesheet
nodes.rationale: Emitting :root custom properties at /theming/{tenantCode}/tokens.css instead of a per-request inline <style> keeps style-src 'self' intact — the CSP is never weakened.
nodes.norm_label: tokens served as an external same-origin stylesheet

nodes.label: draft → validate → preview → publish → rollback/retire
nodes.rationale: Preview is a short-lived, non-indexable, authorized session with a hashed token, X-Robots-Tag: noindex, private/no-store, and a URL namespace distinct from the public stylesheet so it cannot poison the public/CDN cache; every read filters expires_at >= now() so a stale session is inert without a purge job. Published versions are immutable — INSERT-only engine plus a BEFORE UPDATE/DELETE trigger — and rollback/retire only move the active pointer, leaving history intact.

nodes.label: /admin/theming lifecycle console
nodes.rationale: The draft editor is GENERATED from the selected descriptor (one control per declared token/slot/asset slot); a fresh Idempotency-Key per save/publish/rollback/retire click and none on the read-only validate.

nodes.label: workflow_approval module
nodes.rationale: Evolved from a linear step list into a managed, versioned, graph-based workflow minimum while keeping the base guardrail: no domain-specific business terms/actions, no external BPMN engine, and no runtime code execution in conditions/actions.

nodes.label: Closed graph node set (approval/condition/parallel/join/notify/end)
nodes.rationale: A small closed set, never a scripting/expression engine: conditions are either a bounded comparison over a declared fact or a reference to a statically-registered resolver — never both, never neither. validateWorkflowGraph rejects cycles by DFS and runs on every definition write AND again at publish, as defense in depth.

nodes.label: Instance version pinning to the exact definition row
nodes.rationale: Published/active/retired rows are never edited in place (only drafts are editable), so every later read or advance of an instance re-fetches the identical graph regardless of newer versions published afterward.
nodes.norm_label: instance version pinning to the exact definition row

nodes.label: Task-decision serialisation via FOR UPDATE OF t
nodes.rationale: Concurrent decisions on one task are serialised so quorum is never evaluated on a snapshot that cannot see a sibling's in-flight decision; the loser re-reads the winner's committed row, which is what makes the route's status check a correct 409. Chosen over an advisory lock because the lock sits on the very row whose status is the invariant and it also interlocks with cancel/reassign/force-decision/escalation. `OF t` is deliberate — a bare FOR UPDATE would also lock the joined definition row and serialise every instance sharing it.
nodes.norm_label: task-decision serialisation via for update of t

nodes.label: One live seat per person per task (GHSA-9qwq-cmr5-6wfc)
nodes.rationale: A partial unique index is the durable invariant, both assignment INSERT paths are ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, and quorum counts DISTINCT tenant_user_id (people), never rows — without these, someone who was both assignee and escalation target held two seats and could satisfy a 2-person quorum alone. Reassigning to someone who already decided is refused rather than granting a second vote; reassigned/skipped rows sit outside the index predicate so append-only history is unaffected.
nodes.norm_label: one live seat per person per task (ghsa-9qwq-cmr5-6wfc)

nodes.label: Delegation never widens standing
nodes.rationale: A delegation only lets the delegate act with the delegator's OWN standing, never a permission grant and never wider than the row's declared workflowKey/resourceType/effective window; self-approval denial still compares the ACTING user to the instance's original requester, so a delegate cannot approve a request the delegator filed. The audit entry and the domain event are two distinct, independently-consumed records, not the same thing.

nodes.label: Escalation/timeout job idempotency
nodes.rationale: The escalation UPDATE is conditioned on the escalation_step read this pass, so a lost race affects zero rows and is silently skipped rather than double-escalating; the target assignment INSERT is ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING because handing an existing seat-holder a second seat would be a second quorum vote.

nodes.label: Administrative recovery (reassign/cancel/force-decision)
nodes.rationale: Each is permission-gated, reason-required, Idempotency-Keyed and audited, and never overwrites or deletes a prior decision/task/assignment row — only appends or performs a guarded status transition.

nodes.label: force-decision self-approval bypass (fixed pre-merge)
nodes.rationale: The route authorized without populating requestedByTenantUserId while the self-approval-deny check was hardwired to the 'approve' action, so a caller who filed their own instance and held force_decide could force-approve it and bypass quorum entirely. Fixed by looking up the task/instance before the guard and extending the deny check to force_decide.

nodes.label: Self-approval guard vs the generic SoD layer
nodes.rationale: Complementary, not duplicated: the workflow guard is a same-instance creator≠approver check, while the SoD layer enforces registered cross-permission conflicts fail-closed at the shared chokepoint. Caveat carried from the guard's own header: the approve route still calls evaluateAccess directly rather than routing through authorizeInTransaction, so a FUTURE SoD rule naming a workflow permission would need that caller migrated — no active gap today because the base ships zero SoD rules.
nodes.norm_label: self-approval guard vs the generic sod layer

nodes.label: Static condition-resolver / action-handler registry
nodes.rationale: Mirrors domain-event-runtime's consumer registry exactly, and ships one reference resolver and one reference no-op handler to prove the mechanism without inventing business logic. The action-handler registry exists and is tested but NO node type calls it yet — deferred rather than silently dropped.

nodes.label: Low-cardinality workflow metrics
nodes.rationale: All unlabeled or labeled with a fixed code-defined enum only — never a tenant or resource id; per-workflowKey breakdowns would need a bounded-cardinality follow-up, not unbounded labels.

nodes.label: /admin/approvals inbox
nodes.rationale: Cancel lives on the instance panel, not the task row, because cancelling ends the whole instance and every pending task under it — offering it beside one task would misrepresent its blast radius. No definition/graph editor was built: a raw-JSON textarea that accepts a malformed graph until publish rejects it is a worse affordance than none, so the six definition permissions are claimed by no screen and the contract test asserts they stay off.

nodes.label: profile-identity OpenAPI module fragment
nodes.rationale: Owns every path carrying this module's tag plus schemas referenced ONLY by its operations; schemas shared by 2+ modules live in the root fragment. NOT independently valid OpenAPI — cross-fragment $refs resolve only after openapi:bundle merges it, so the generated bundle must never be hand-edited.

nodes.label: Office CRUD + soft-delete/restore operations
nodes.rationale: Keyset-paginated listing, newest first; delete is audited and restorable rather than destructive.

nodes.label: postSetupInitialize — one-time bootstrap
nodes.rationale: Bootstraps the first tenant, owner, office, role and access assignment in one call and is rejected once already locked.

nodes.label: provisionTenant / listTenants — PLATFORM-scoped
nodes.rationale: Explicitly platform-scoped rather than tenant-scoped — these operations cross the tenant boundary by design.

nodes.label: Frozen awcms-astro consumer contract (ADR-0065)
nodes.rationale: Generated, never hand-edited. Regenerating is a DELIBERATE act meaning 'this contract changed and the consumer must change with it' — the awcms-astro side has to be updated in the same breath, since that repo's build is what this file exists to stop breaking silently. The check is a SUBSET assertion, so additive changes (a new optional field, a new enum value) already pass and need no regeneration.

nodes.label: accessIssueMachineCredential operation
nodes.rationale: Returns the plaintext token exactly once; authenticates only, with module-enabled/RBAC/ABAC/SoD still applying; allowedPermissionKeys narrows by intersection so granting the service account another role never widens an issued credential; refused unless the action is read-only; deliberately not idempotency-keyed because replaying would mean persisting the plaintext.

nodes.label: example-domain-modules test-support fixture
nodes.rationale: Illustrative domain modules used ONLY by tests to exercise the base's enforcement engines against realistic module metadata the base registry deliberately does not ship; never registered in src/modules/index.ts.

nodes.label: example_crm example domain module
nodes.rationale: Carries five-plus illustrative SoD rules, an OpenAPI fragment, permissions, navigation and a job — enough to prove every composition check runs on a domain module, while the base itself ships ZERO SoD rules. Since ADR-0060 it no longer declares business_scope_hierarchy, because tenant_admin owns that capability in the base.

nodes.label: Dummy in-memory BusinessScopeHierarchyPort resolver
nodes.rationale: Resolves exact/descendant/ancestor over an in-memory graph with tenant isolation, depth bounds and cycle detection — heterogeneous ancestry testable without a real domain module or DB table.

nodes.label: extraFragmentFiles OpenAPI merge seam
nodes.rationale: Proves an additional fragment merges into the bundle without editing base fragments, and that a fragment colliding on a base path/schema is rejected with BundleConflictError.
